newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - Aug 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet : lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
MORE THAN 200 TAMIL TIGERS KILLED IN BATTLE

More than 200 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels were killed and an equal number wounded in a battle in Sri Lanka's northern Wanni region. Thirty-five police, 19 army and 13 navy personnel were also killed in the attack, the third mounted by the rebels since the army launched a major offensive in May to open a strategic highway to link Jaffna peninsula with the rest of the island.
TAMIL MPs UNHAPPY OVER REJECTION OF DEVELOPMENT PROPOSALS

Tamil lawmakers are unhappy over rejection of several district development plans put by them to the Ministry of Plan Implementation under the decentralised budget allocations. Lawmakers said the ministry regularly rejected their proposals on the pretext that they were meant for areas which were not under government control.
REFERENDUM ON CONSTITUTION EXPECTED IN OCTOBER

The government proposes to hold a referendum in October to assess the views of the public on the constitutional proposals put forward by the government to find a permanent solution to the ethnic issue. Officials of the presidential secretariat are finalising dates for public meetings to be addressed by President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
SLFP MOSLEMS DEMAND SAY IN PARLIAMENTARY SELECT COMMITTE

Moslem members of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party, the main constituent of the ruling People's Alliance governemnt, have demanded that they be included in the deliberations of the parliamentary select committee debating the new constitution. They said Sri Lanka's Moslem parties usually projected their own interests and not the community's.
